findings.title: 78 FormRequests still bypass authorization via return true; (plan claim 86 unverified by my evidence)
findings.evidence: Body-of-authorize() scan with awk extraction yields 78 files where authorize() contains 'return true;'. Plan claims 86 — likely counted files where 'return true;' appears anywhere (e.g., in validation closures or rules). Both numbers establish the same gap, but 78 is the load-bearing count. Wave 5H closed 5/~83 (CurrencyRequest, TaxRequest, BranchRequest, RoleRequest, AdministratorRequest). Sample 10 verified naked: ItemRequest:18-21, CouponRequest:17-20, OfferRequest:16-19, NotificationRequest:15-18, ItemCategoryRequest:15-18, ItemAttributeRequest:15-18, KioskMachineRequest:13-16, CustomerRequest:16-19, EmployeeRequest:16-19, ChefRequest:16-19, DeliveryBoyRequest:16-19, WaiterRequest:16-19, ChangePasswordRequest:15-18, Admin/PaymentTerminalRequest:11-14, SmsGatewayRequest:14-17. CONTEXT: 65/80 Admin controllers carry permission:* middleware in constructor — so FormRequest::authorize gap is partly mitigated. But 15 admin controllers have ZERO permission middleware (see PR-D-F11).
findings.blast_radius: Any role with API access can POST/PUT/DELETE these 78 endpoints IF the corresponding controller lacks permission:* in constructor. Concrete examples: Notification settings update by any waiter; Kiosk machine pairing by any role; SMS gateway config change by any staff.
findings.remediation: Plan T3 top-8 cluster (Item/Coupon/ItemCategory/ItemAttribute/Offer/Notification/PaymentGateway/KioskMachine). Pattern from AdministratorRequest:22-26 ($user?->can('<cap>') ?? false). PR-D2/D3/D4 sweep for remaining ~70.

findings.title: Password policy min:6 across all user-creation/update endpoints
findings.evidence: 9 FormRequest files (1 more than plan F-D4's 8 — CustomerRequest:48 also has min:6) confirm string|min:6. Wave 5G raised bcrypt rounds 10→12 but didn't touch entropy minimum. NIST SP 800-63B recommends min 8 (with composition); OWASP 2023 recommends min 12.
findings.blast_radius: Brute-force trivial against bcrypt(12) at min:6 entropy (~30 bits) for an admin account. Restaurant staff have weak password culture (default 'cayenne1' or '123456'). NF525 audit-chain access keyed on admin login — credential theft = forensic chain compromise.
findings.remediation: Plan T5 — replace 'string', 'min:6' with Password::min(12)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() (Password rule). Apply ONLY to store/update FormRequests, NOT to login/check (existing weak hashes still validate via bcrypt rehash from Wave 5G).

Zero admin routes (Currency/Tax/Branch/Notification/PushNotification/Coupon/Item/Offer store/destroy etc.) marked required. routes/api.php grep confirms idempotency middleware only attached to POS+cash+kiosk lines (728, 768, 788, 799, 800, 813, 817, 820, 824, 859, 861, 868, 879, 880, 889, 1131, 1134) — admin store/destroy never carries idempotency.

findings.remediation: Plan T4 — flip env default OFF→ON SAFE-ROLLOUT by adding 12 admin routes to required_routes (still opt-in pattern preserved at middleware:163). Frozen IdempotencyKeyMiddleware UNTOUCHED — config-only change.

findings.title: Customer extends User — BranchScope on Customer would trigger Sanctum recursion (plan T7 list contains Customer; must be excluded)
findings.evidence: Customer.php:9 — class Customer extends User. BranchScope.php:21-23 — explicitly returns early if model instanceof User to avoid 'BranchScope ↔ Sanctum infinite recursion' (file comment line 20). Since Customer extends User, the instanceof check WOULD pass and exempt Customer too, IF developer added scope via addGlobalScope on Customer's booted(). BUT — Eloquent runs each model's booted() independently; adding scope on Customer would call apply() with $model = Customer instance, and $model instanceof User === true (PHP inheritance), so the apply() short-circuits at line 21 and does nothing. Net result: NO recursion bug, but ALSO NO scoping applied — silent no-op.
findings.blast_radius: If executor adds BranchScope on Customer thinking it filters, silent failure — Customer queries remain unscoped. Worse, executor may experiment with custom scope that DOES filter and trigger Sanctum recursion via Customer::login path.
findings.remediation: Plan correction: Remove Customer from T7 list. If cross-branch Customer visibility is a real risk, use explicit ::query()->where('branch_id', auth()->user()->branch_id) in CustomerController, not global scope.

findings.title: 15 admin controllers carry zero permission:* middleware (NEW finding, not in plan)
findings.evidence: ls Admin controllers excl POS/Kiosk/KDS/OSS = 80 files. grep -L 'permission:' = 15. routes/api.php admin group (line 269) only carries [installed, apiKey, auth:sanctum, localization, throttle:admin-mutation] — no permission:* group middleware. routes/api.php has ONLY 3 inline permission:* references (lines 682, 696, 718) for ingredients + catalog.compose + catalog.publish. So 15 controllers depend ENTIRELY on FormRequest::authorize() — most of which return true (F-F5).
findings.blast_radius: ComposerProfileController + ComposerStepController + IngredientController mutate the catalog wizard config — critical Cayenne composer profiles + ingredient mapping. MenuController + MenuSection + MenuTemplate modify menu structure. AddressController + DefaultAccessController + AnalyticSection + CountryCode + Timezone are less critical but still no gate. ComposerProfile + ComposerStep should use catalog.publish (already a Spatie permission per ComposerPermissionsMinimalSeeder.php:11). Add 'menu_manage', 'address_manage', 'analytics_manage' permissions if not seeded. NEW finding — add to PR-D as T9 (small) or split to PR-D2.

findings.title: Idempotency middleware silently treats route-name OR URI-pattern matching (defense-in-depth ambiguity)
findings.evidence: isRouteRequired() iterates required_routes; matches either 'name:foo' (line 169) OR $request->is(pattern) (line 175). config/idempotency.php uses URI patterns like 'api/admin/pos'. POS+kiosk routes might have been renamed; orphan patterns silently fail-safe (treats as not-required, header-absent passes through).
findings.blast_radius: Operational drift — adding new route in routes/api.php with name() but no URI-pattern match could leave the route uncovered even if executor thinks idempotency is applied via name reference. Audit suggests prefer name: prefix.
findings.remediation: Plan T4 follow-up — when adding 12 admin routes, prefer 'name:admin.currency.store' over 'api/admin/currency'. Frozen IdempotencyKeyMiddleware.php logic UNTOUCHED.
